tagline: North along a band of hills the wind built.
intro: From the Missouri line below Hamburg the byway runs north 220 paved miles to Akron, along the first rise of land east of the Missouri River floodplain. The hills are loess, fine silt the wind lifted off drying mud flats as the last glaciers melted and piled into a band some 200 miles long. To see taller loess, the state tourism office notes, a traveler would have to go to China.

Dry loess stands in vertical columns, so the hills have worn into razor ridges, some under ten feet wide with sixty-foot drops on either side, and slumped into cat-step terraces. Locals call it sugar clay.

moments.title: Tabor
moments.text: Abolitionists settled this high ground in 1852. Two hundred Sharps rifles bound for Kansas waited in a minister's barn, and John Brown wintered here training men for Harpers Ferry.

moments.title: Preparation Canyon State Park
moments.text: Settlers who named their town Preparation, for the world to come, fell out with their leader, Father Ephraim, before the Iowa Supreme Court. He fled the state. The canyon kept the name.

moments.title: Sergeant Floyd Monument
moments.text: Sergeant Charles Floyd of the Lewis and Clark expedition was buried on this Missouri River bluff in 1804. The river took part of the grave, so he was moved back from the edge.

practical: Beyond the paved main route are 185 miles of optional excursion loops, some of them on gravel.
